title: offline-artifact-staging-kms-rotation-multi-site-rollup-contract
creator: Maya Patel
description: Define unambiguous requirements and acceptance criteria for upgrades and key rotations in Private/VPC (including air-gapped) deployments. Focus areas: offline artifact staging and verification, KMS/HSM rotation windows and constraints, and multi-site rolling upgrade contracts that guarantee safe canaries and rollback paths without requiring outbound egress.
background: Several recent Private deployment upgrades highlighted two recurring risks: (1) artifact mirror divergence in air-gapped sites leading to failed image verification during upgrades, and (2) KMS/HSM rotation procedures that assume intermittent outbound connectivity. This ticket consolidates product-level requirements and operational acceptance criteria so Engineering, Security, and Solutions can agree on contract guarantees provided to customers during upgrades.
requirements: Offline artifact staging must support a signed manifest format (SHA256 per artifact + RPM/OCI digest) that operators can validate locally before upgrades.
Upgrade orchestration must be able to run with zero outbound egress. All necessary artifacts and manifests must be pre-seeded into an operator-controlled registry or local mirror.
KMS/HSM rotation workflows must include an offline-compatible mode: signed rotation manifests, operator approval step, and optional manual key import for HSMs without remote KMS connectivity.

Canary strategy must be defined at two levels: pod-level canaries within a cluster, and site-level canaries across isolated VPCs/air-gapped locations. Each canary must include health checks, latency baselines, and traffic guardrails.
Upgrade time windows and preflight checks must include cluster-level quotas, disk space checks, node kubelet and runtime compatibility, and manifest signature validation.
Rollbacks must be automatable via operator commands if an upgrade fails to meet SLOs or manifest verification fails; operator must be able to revert without accessing external registries.
Audit logging requirements: every upgrade and KMS rotation must emit a signed audit record stored locally and optionally pushed to the customer's SIEM during the next allowed egress window.
Operator UX: console and CLI must expose explicit 'offline validation' output with clear pass/fail reasons for each preflight check to reduce on-site troubleshooting time.
acceptance_criteria: Given a fully air-gapped cluster with pre-seeded artifact mirror, running the upgrade operator with --offline-verify succeeds and returns a signed success manifest. (Test: local lab cluster)

Given a customer HSM that cannot reach Redwood KMS endpoint, the rotation workflow completes using signed rotation manifests and manual key-seed instructions without exposing plaintext keys. (Test: HSM integration lab)

A staged canary across two isolated sites validates new runtime for 48h with no regression in 99th percentile latency (> baseline) and zero dropped requests; if metrics exceed thresholds, the operator automatically halts rollout and records signed audit events. (Simulated traffic test)
If an artifact manifest mismatch occurs during preflight, the operator fails fast with non-ambiguous remediation steps and does not start the upgrade. (Negative test)

Every upgrade run produces an immutable, signed audit artifact stored in /var/lib/redwood/audits with UUID and hash, and the operator exposes commands to export these artifacts for customer-side ingestion. (Operational check)
Upgrade operators support a dry-run that exercises all preflight checks and outputs a machine-readable checklist (JSON) that can be used by automation before the live rollout. (CLI/Console feature)
upgrade_runbook: Day 0: Prepare pre-seeded mirror — generate signed manifest (sha256 + timestamp) and copy artifacts via approved transfer method (sneakernet / airgapped proxy).
Day 1: Run operator --dry-run --offline-verify to validate manifests, disk, and runtime compatibility; collect JSON checklist output; confirm with on-site operator.
Day 2: Start pod-level canary on 1-2 nodes with traffic steering (10% traffic) for 2 hours; monitor latency/CPU/RPS and custom health checks; if pass, proceed to site-level canary.
Day 3: Site-level canary in a second isolated VPC for 48 hours with full telemetry capture; if metrics meet thresholds, proceed to rolling upgrade (20% increments).
If at any stage a threshold fails, run redwood operator rollback --to-manifest <previous-manifest-id> and collect local audit artifact; escalate to on-call and follow incident checklist.
rollback_criteria: Must be executable without external artifact fetch. Rollback uses local mirror and previous signed manifest.
Rollback must complete within the documented RTO for the customer tier (Dedicated: 30 minutes for pod-level rollback; Private: 2 hours site-level rollback).
Operator must verify post-rollback integrity by re-running offline-verify and produce a signed audit record.
test_plan: Integration lab: create two air-gapped clusters (cluster-A, cluster-B) with mirrored artifacts and run full upgrade flow including KMS rotation in offline mode.
Chaos test: during site-level canary, inject node reboots and network partition to validate canary holds and rollback triggers.
HSM test: simulate HSM that only supports manual key import — verify rotation manifests and operator guidance lead to successful key rotation without contacting Redwood KMS.
Manifest-mismatch negative test: alter artifact digest in mirror and confirm operator halts upgrade with clear remediation output.
audit_and_kms_rotation: Rotation manifests must be signed with a Redwood rotation signing key and verifiable by the operator using a bundled public key.
Rotation workflow must support manual HSM import instructions and provide a verification API that validates key material fingerprint without sending secrets outbound.
Audit artifacts must include: operator identity, manifest id, start/end timestamps, success/failure status, and a signature.
review_feedback: Security: require a separate signing key for rotation manifests; do not reuse release artifact signing key.
Solutions Eng: add a pre-approved transfer checklist for on-site technicians and a downloadable verification tool for customers.
Eng (runtime): ensure the operator's image footprint for air-gapped mode is <200MB to accommodate constrained mirrors.
notes: This ticket consolidates multiple customer asks after Pilot X and Y where on-site operators lacked clear rollback instructions.
We will coordinate a 2-week engineering spike to build the offline verification tooling; deliverables include a CLI --offline-verify and a JSON checklist output for automation.
Plan for a joint runbook review session with Security and Solutions on 2026-03-18.
